ytui now draws every video one way: 24-bit colour glyphs over a dimmed copy of the picture, in two modes, **glow** (the default) and **braille**. Glow is translated from [react-video-ascii](https://github.com/LucasHJin/react-video-ascii) by Lucas Jin. Website and docs: https://bong-water-water-bong.github.io/ytui/

## Download

| Platform | Package | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `ytui-v2026.10.17-windows-x86_64.zip` | Unzip and run `ytui.exe` in **Windows Terminal**. |
| Linux (x86_64) | `ytui-v2026.10.17-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `ytui-v2026.10.17-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | |

Each package holds `ytui` (or `ytui.exe`), `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`. You also need `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg` and a JavaScript runtime (`deno` or Node.js) on your PATH, and a truecolour terminal. On Windows: `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp Gyan.FFmpeg DenoLand.Deno`.

Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## What's new

- **Two render modes, both 24-bit colour.** `m` switches between them; `o` opens the look panel (brightness, saturation, background, contrast, auto-exposure); `[ ]` change contrast.
  - **glow** (default): shape-matched ASCII in boosted colour, translated from react-video-ascii's shaders. It picks the same characters as the [demo](https://video-ascii-demo.vercel.app/), with the demo's look (brightness and saturation 1.25, background 0.30), on every system and with no font file.
  - **braille**: 2x4 dots that light up with the picture's brightness and follow its edges. Dots and ground each take their own part of the cell's colour.
- **One player:** every video plays through ffmpeg, up to 720p at 60 fps, and is drawn in the terminal.
- **Sound on Linux with PipeWire:** fixed; audio played silently where `pw-cat` was installed.
- **Captions** (`S`) now come straight from YouTube's caption files, drawn as text over the video.
- **Sign in with Firefox:** if you're signed in to YouTube in Firefox, ytui takes that sign-in at once; otherwise it opens Google's sign-in page as a Firefox tab and finishes by itself. Set `YTUI_BROWSER=firefox` to prefer Firefox over Chrome, Edge, Brave and Chromium.
- **`ytui --uninstall`:** signs you out of Google, then removes ytui's settings, data and cache, and ytui itself. It lists everything first and asks before deleting (`--yes` skips the question).
- **Website and docs:** install guides, render modes, playback, sign-in, keys, options, troubleshooting, and a guide to watching YouTube in the terminal, including over SSH and in tmux.
- **Fix:** the sign-in window opens from a tmux session started outside the desktop.

## Removed

To keep ytui simple, these are gone: libmpv and the native and mpv video windows (`N`, `--engine`, `--no-native`), kitty and sixel graphics (`G`, `--gfx*`, `--sixel-colors`), the 3D engine, `--demo3d` and the visualiser (`V`), the other render modes (art, ascii, classic, sextant, quadrant, halfblock), and the 256-colour fallback. The Windows package no longer bundles libmpv.

## Credits

Glow and braille follow [react-video-ascii](https://github.com/LucasHJin/react-video-ascii) by Lucas Jin (MIT, [demo](https://video-ascii-demo.vercel.app/)). Its licence is in `NOTICE`.
